claim: LLM microserving exposes fine-grained sub-request-level REST primitives (prep_recv, remote_send, start_generate) so a programmable router can implement disaggregation strategies as plain async Python against a list of abstract engine objects, rather than being hard-coded to a specific orchestration substrate.
stance_target: router logic can be written against a backend abstraction fully decoupled from how backend instances are deployed (K8s or otherwise)
quoted_support: A programmable router transforms user requests into sub-request calls, enabling the dynamic reconfiguration of serving patterns.

claim: A novel 1P1D-balance disaggregation strategy, expressible in the microserving router in a few lines of code, reduces job completion time by up to 47% compared to existing static disaggregation strategies.
stance_target: fine-grained router-level programmability yields measurable performance gains over fixed-strategy routers
scope_conditions: Llama 3.1 8B, single NVIDIA A100 SXM 40GB per engine, ShareGPT and synthetic long-context workloads, vLLM v0.6.3.post1 baseline
quoted_support: Additionally, it allows us to explore new strategy variants that reduce up to 47% of job completion time compared to the existing strategies.

claim: The evaluation used a Poisson-sampled request arrival process at different per-GPU rates specifically to fairly compare disaggregation patterns that use different total GPU counts (1P1D vs 1P2D), and reported TTFT, TPOT, and JCT as the metrics.
quoted_support: The request arrival follows the arrival time sampled from the Poisson distribution of different per-GPU request rates, in order to fairly compare disaggregation patterns that use different numbers of GPUs.

claim: Most production LLM inference services expose only a coarse-grained request-level REST API with a fixed, pre-configured coordination strategy baked in at startup, so changing the coordination strategy requires reconfiguring and restarting the underlying system, disrupting production.
stance_target: motivation for building a router against a fine-grained backend abstraction instead of a coarse request-level API
scope_conditions: general critique of pre-2024 LLM serving system design
quoted_support: Changing the strategy usually involves reconfiguring the underlying system and restarting the service, causing disruptions to the production environment.
